messages:
maria.g: Heads up — spot preemptions in us-west2 spiked overnight (~30% eviction on p4-spot pool). Our batch queues lagging behind and some interactive requests hit cold-start. Anyone else seeing this?
ryan: saw it in metrics. Preemptions peaked around 03:20 UTC, sustained for ~40m. Cost saved but throughput tanked. :grimacing:
tara: same. Notebook users reported longer token latency. We've got low-priority batch jobs competing with retrain pipelines.
lee: question — do we have a fallback policy for tiered queues? We should reserve a small on-demand pool for interactive / high-priority pods and force-checkpoint batch jobs to tolerate interruptions.
oncall-sre: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) cordon high-latency spot nodes, 2) bump reserved pool from 5% -> 12% until morning, 3) enable graceful eviction hooks for long-running jobs.
autoscale-bot: Alert: ClusterAutoscaler scaled down spot-pool by 28 nodes between 03:10-03:45 due to preemptions. No errors in scale events.
ryan: For longer term: we should classify workloads into 3 buckets: interactive-high, batch-resumable, batch-ephemeral. Map them to capacity classes: reserved, mixed (spot+on-demand), spot-only.
tara: Agreed. Also we need better checkpointing for 'batch-resumable' — add a preemption handler that uploads checkpoint to GCS/S3 every N minutes. Example snippet we used before:```bash
trap 'checkpoint && exit' TERM
while training; do
  save_checkpoint s3://redwood-checkpoints/$JOB_ID
  sleep 600
done
```
lee: We should implement scheduling priorities via PriorityClass and PodTopologies + gang scheduling for multi-gpu jobs to avoid partial starts. Example: `priorityClassName: interactive-high` for user-facing, `preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority` for k8s pods.
oncall-sre: Also start labeling spot nodes with `spot=true` and use nodeAffinity / tolerations to steer. For mixed pools, autoscaler needs separate min/max per pool and a fallback pool with instant warm GPUs.
maria.g: Can we also try an off-peak shift window for non-urgent batch? e.g., preferentially schedule heavy RLhf/long retrains 01:00-05:00 local region to exploit lower spot churn. We can add a simple cron to enqueue those jobs into a low-priority queue.
ryan: Good idea — schedule window + dynamic throttling. We'll need a metric for preemption-rate by hour+zone to automate that. I'll add a dash widget: `preempt_rate{zone=`
